parts.markdown:
Use our free **Iowa paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Iowa income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other payroll deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Iowa's flat income tax rate simplifies part of the paycheck calculation. However, household income, withholding allowances and employee deductions still influence the final amount.

Whether you work in Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, Davenport, Iowa City or another Iowa community, understanding your net income can help you compare salary offers and manage monthly expenses.

## How to Use the Iowa Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary if you receive fixed compensation or hourly wages if your earnings depend on working hours.

Enter your gross income before taxes and select your pay frequency.

Enter federal and Iowa income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions, healthcare premiums, additional withholding and other payroll deductions.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual taxes and remaining net earnings.

For greater accuracy, use your most recent pay stub and withholding certificate.

## Iowa Payroll Taxes in 2026

Iowa employees generally encounter federal and state income taxes alongside ordinary payroll contributions.

## How Iowa State Income Tax Works

Iowa applies a flat individual income tax rate of 3.8% in 2026.

However, this rate should not simply be multiplied by your gross paycheck.

Iowa's payroll withholding procedure accounts for the appropriate deduction based on withholding status. The resulting tax amount is further adjusted by the employee's withholding allowances and any additional requested withholding.

This means employees receiving identical salaries may have different state deductions depending on their household circumstances.

The [Iowa 2026 withholding tax information](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/withholding-tax/iowa-withholding-tax-information/2026-withholding-tax-information) provides the applicable employer tables and calculation instructions.

## How to Calculate Iowa Income Tax Withholding

Iowa's payroll calculation involves four main operations.

First, subtract the appropriate pay-period deduction from taxable wages.

Next, apply the 3.8% withholding rate.

Subtract the employee's annual withholding allowance divided by the number of annual pay periods.

Finally, include any additional withholding requested for the current paycheck.

### Iowa withholding example

Suppose an employee receives $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages, qualifies for a $500 pay-period deduction and has a $40 annual withholding allowance.

Adjusted taxable wages:

$2,500 − $500 = $2,000

Tax before the allowance adjustment:

$2,000 × 3.8% = $76

Allowance adjustment:

$40 ÷ 26 = approximately $1.54

Estimated Iowa withholding:

$76 − $1.54 = $74.46

If the employee requests another $10 in state withholding, the total would be approximately $84.46.

This example assumes ordinary payroll circumstances and uses cents for illustrative precision.

## Understanding Iowa Form IA W-4

Iowa employees use Form IA W-4 to provide state withholding information to their employers.

More recent versions of the form use a total dollar allowance amount rather than simply requiring the employee to report a number of allowances.

Employees with forms from 2023 or earlier may require a conversion. Under the 2026 withholding methodology, each applicable old-form allowance is converted into a $40 annual allowance amount.

For instance, six allowances on an older form would correspond to an annual allowance amount of $240.

This distinction matters because entering six dollars instead of six allowances would produce an inaccurate result.

Review your withholding certificate and update it when your employment or household circumstances change.

## Iowa Withholding for Married Couples With Two Incomes

Married couples with two working spouses may need to pay particular attention to withholding.

If both employers calculate deductions independently, the combined household withholding may be insufficient to cover the family's final income tax liability.

Employees may need to adjust their state withholding selections or request additional withholding.

A higher monthly take-home paycheck can be useful, but not if it creates an unexpected tax bill at the end of the year.

Review your estimated household income and existing withholding before changing your elections.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Iowa Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal withholding depends on taxable wages, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

The calculation may account for filing status, multiple jobs, eligible credits, deductions and additional withholding requests.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered Social Security wages up to the 2026 annual limit of $184,500.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Additional Medicare withholding generally applies at 0.9% once covered wages paid by an employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for federal income tax withholding procedures.

Assume the employee has the same Iowa withholding settings used in the earlier example, no pre-tax deductions and no additional requested withholding.

Your actual net paycheck depends on your federal withholding information and employee benefits.

## Iowa Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate their gross wages using regular and qualifying overtime hours.

Suppose an employee earns $24 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $24 × 40 = $960

Overtime earnings: $24 × 1.5 × 6 = $216

Total gross earnings: $1,176

Applicable federal and Iowa taxes are then calculated from their respective taxable wage amounts.

Employees receiving commissions, bonuses or other supplemental compensation may experience different withholding treatment.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about overtime eligibility.

## Does Iowa Have Local Income Taxes?

Iowa residents in certain school districts may owe a school district income surtax through their annual income tax return.

This should not automatically be treated as a standard municipal wage tax deducted from every paycheck.

Employees should distinguish regular payroll withholding from additional taxes that may be assessed when filing their annual return.

The applicable school district surtax depends on residency and the district's tax requirements.

If you expect an additional tax liability, consider whether adjusting your regular withholding or establishing a separate savings reserve would be appropriate.

## Working in Iowa and Living in Illinois

Iowa and Illinois have a reciprocal income tax agreement covering qualifying employee compensation.

Eligible employees working across the state border may generally pay state income tax to their residence state rather than their employment state.

The appropriate withholding exemption certificate must be provided where required.

Employees working in other neighboring states should not assume that the same reciprocity agreement applies.

Consult the Iowa Department of Revenue for guidance before claiming a nonresident withholding exemption.

## Managing Your Iowa Take-Home Pay

Build your monthly budget using estimated net income rather than gross annual salary.

Account for housing, groceries, transportation, insurance and required debt payments.

When comparing jobs, include differences in healthcare premiums, retirement matching, paid leave and commuting expenses.

Our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare different employment arrangements, while our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Iowa's income tax rate in 2026?

Iowa's individual income tax rate is 3.8%. Actual paycheck withholding depends on taxable wages, the applicable deduction and withholding allowances.

### Does my spouse's income affect Iowa withholding?

Yes. The applicable Iowa withholding deduction can differ depending on whether a spouse also has earned income.

### Do Iowa school district surtaxes come out of every paycheck?

School district surtaxes are generally assessed through the annual income tax return rather than automatically withheld as an ordinary local payroll income tax.
